en: The Sūtra of the Secret Heart Dhāraṇī of the Noble Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, King of Non-Vainness,
translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, Chao Feng Da Fu, Acting Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
Translated by the Dharma Master Śīladhara, recipient of the purple robe and subject, and others, by imperial decree: Thus have I heard.
At one time, the World-Honored One was dwelling in the palace of the Holy Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva on Mount Potalaka.
There were countless great sāla trees,
tamāla trees, campaka trees, aśoka trees, and atimuktaka trees.
Thus, it was adorned with various kinds of such jewel-trees.
He was accompanied by a great assembly of one million eight hundred thousand bhikṣus and ninety koṭi-nayuta-hundred-thousand bodhisattvas.
Furthermore, there were the Brahmā-sons such as Īśvara and Maheśvara,
as well as hundreds of thousands of countless *viśuddhaprabha* devaputras;
this assembly thus respectfully surrounded him as he listened to and received his teaching of the Dharma.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Noble Avalokiteśvara rose from his seat,
bared his right shoulder, knelt with his right knee on the ground,
and, facing the Buddha, joined his palms in reverence and prostrated himself before him.
With a joyful and smiling countenance, he came forward and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, I possess a dhāraṇī named 'King of Non-Emptiness' (Amogharāja), which is the secret heart-mantra.
In the past, ninety-one kalpas ago..."
I personally heard and received this from the Tathāgata Avalokiteśvararāja while he was universally surveying the worlds.
At that time, that Tathāgata was for the sake of countless hundreds of thousands of Brahmā sons and the assembly of the Pure Radiance (Vimalaprabha) deva sons.
He taught me the Dharma of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
At that time, I realized hundreds of thousands of samādhi-doors, such as the "Non-empty Wisdom" (Aśūnyajñāna).
Blessed One, in whatever place this Secret Heart Dhāraṇī is proclaimed and circulated,
you should know that twelve thousand devaputras, including Maheśvara and others, will secretly provide protection for that place.
That place shall be equivalent to having various stūpas of the Buddhas;
one should honor, revere, and make offerings to it with respect.
Furthermore, if there is anyone who widely disseminates this Secret Heart Dhāraṇī of the Amoghapāśa King, [they shall likewise receive such merit].
One should know that such a person has already deeply planted roots of goodness under countless hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of buddhas.
Furthermore, if there is anyone who even briefly hears this dhāraṇī, [they shall likewise attain great merit].
Even if such a person should further slander the Buddha, slander the Dharma,
and slander the various worthies and sages, including bodhisattvas, śrāvakas, and pratyekabuddhas,
they would extensively create such extremely grave karmic offenses.
If those who are destined to fall into the Avīci Hell can,
with a sincere mind, fast for one day and recite this dhāraṇī according to the ritual rules, [they shall be saved].
In this way, all such sins shall be extinguished.
Furthermore, if there is anyone suffering from various types of malaria—
whether it recurs every day, every two days, or even up to every seven days.
Or again, there may be pain in the eyes, ears, nose, or head;
or again, there may be scabies, sores, ringworm, carbuncles, abscesses, swellings, or blisters;
or one may be afflicted by all manner of non-human beings and malevolent spirits.
Possession by spirits, seizing and grasping, binding with spells, beating and hurling,
cursing, threatening, and deluding with false doctrines—
to speak briefly, these are all such things.
By the power of the empowerment of this dhāraṇī, all physical and mental illnesses,
and even inauspicious things seen in dreams,
shall be completely gathered and eliminated.
All shall be completely extinguished so that they can no longer cause harm.
Furthermore, World-Honored One, if among those of the kṣatriya, brāhmaṇa, vaiśya, or śūdra castes— within such lineages—
there should be those with a deceitful and hypocritical mind, [may their afflictions likewise be extinguished].
Regarding this dhāraṇī, it is permitted for them to hear, receive, transcribe, read, and recite it;
even for all those of various species among the animals,
one should likewise recite this dhāraṇī for them so that they may hear it.
Having heard it, all shall obtain benefit according to their respective capacities;
how much more so for those monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen who give rise to a mind of pure faith and understanding.
Listen with a sincere mind to this dhāraṇī.
Furthermore, if there are those who contemplate these secret verses of the dhāraṇī with a concentrated mind.
At that time, one should remain free from all faults;
that is to say, one should neither disparage nor praise, and should not give rise to doubt or suspicion.
One should cultivate a mind free from the notion of "self" and a mind devoid of concern for duration or proximity.
With a mind free from contrivance, a mind free from defilement, and a mind free from pride or inferiority,
one dwells in such a state of mind while performing the visualization of the Buddha.
That person will immediately see a thousand Buddhas appearing before them in each of the ten directions.
Blessed One, if within the house of any layperson there is this dhāraṇī sūtra,
whether the master or the servants see this sūtra, [they shall be protected].
Even if they should give rise to contempt or engage in jesting,
by the power of my majestic spiritual authority,
may they naturally hear the sound of this dhāraṇī.
World-Honored One, it is as if there were someone who takes sandalwood, or camphor,
or musk, and beats it, or chops and minces it.
Furthermore, he performed incantations with mantras as curses,
and then ground [the substance] upon a coarse,
rugged stone to smear it upon his body.
Some may say: "There is no need for beating, cutting, chopping, chanting incantations over, or grinding;
once fragrances such as sandalwood have already been applied to the body."
That fragrance remains ever-present.
World-Honored One, this Secret Heart Dhāraṇī of the Amoghapāśa King is likewise:
even if there should be someone who treats it with contempt or mocks it in jest, [it shall still bring its benefits].
Even those who lack a heart of sincerity,
yet are able to make offerings to this dhāraṇī—
by the power of the roots of goodness from such offerings, those persons [shall attain liberation].
In every lifetime they are born, they shall always obtain morality, meditative concentration, wisdom, and so forth;
their aggregates shall be fully endowed with a wondrous and fragrant aroma.
Furthermore, if there are bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās, and so on—
When one wishes to receive and uphold this Amoghapāśa-hṛdaya-mantra, one should,
on the eighth day of the waxing moon, arrange the ritual mandala according to the dharma and perform offerings.
The practitioner must maintain purity and abstain from food.
With a mind free of conceptual attachment, they should recite this Secret Heart Dhāraṇī seven times.
This person shall obtain twenty kinds of merit.
First, one shall be born into wealth and nobility;
second, once born, all karmic diseases from past lives shall be swiftly extinguished;
third, one shall always possess a body that is fine, smooth, and exquisitely beautiful.
First, their sense faculties are concealed and they are beloved by others;
second, they obtain great wealth and profit;
third, all their treasures and possessions cannot be stolen.
Sixth, all one's wealth and treasures shall not be consumed by fire or swept away by water.
Seventh, one will constantly find that one's fields expand and increase.
Eighth, the crops in those fields shall not be damaged by thunder or hail.
Ninth, their fields will not be ravaged by evil rains or prolonged deluges.
Tenth, their physical appearance, vitality, and mental spirit will suffer no depletion.
Eleventh, they will always be respected and cherished by all sentient beings.
Twelfth, they are not terrified by any adversaries.
Thirteenth, should there be adversaries, they are swiftly resolved and eliminated.
Fourteenth, they are not terrified by any non-human beings.
Fifteenth, they will not be bound by malignant diseases.
Sixteenth, they will not be terrified by ḍākinīs.
Seventeenth, they will remain far removed from all matters pertaining to the afflictions (*kleśa*).
Eighteenth, one shall not die by water, fire, weapons, or poison.
Nineteenth, wherever one may be, one will always receive secret protection from the various worthies and sages.
Twentieth: wherever one is born, one shall always not be separated from loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity.
These are called the twenty kinds of merit.
Furthermore, World-Honored One, if there be anyone who upholds and recites this dhāraṇī...
One further attains eight kinds of auspicious signs:
first, at the time of death, I shall appear before them in the form of a bhikṣu;
second, at the time of death, their eyes will not be agitated or distracted, and their body and mind will remain peaceful and stable.
Third, at the time of death, their hands do not clutch at empty space and their feet do not kick the ground;
furthermore, they are not defiled by the mess of excrement or urine.
Fourth, they do not die with their faces covered.
Fifth, at the time of death, one dwells securely in right mindfulness.
Sixth, at the time of death, one is not separated from virtuous friends.
Seventh, after the end of life, one is reborn in accordance with one's vows within the buddha-fields.
Eighth, one shall obtain inexhaustible eloquence upon birth.
These are called the eight kinds of auspicious signs.
Furthermore, World-Honored One:
If there is anyone who can maintain purity by abstaining from food,
remaining far removed from the five pungent roots and all types of meat or impure substances,
and recites this dhāraṇī three times during each of the three periods of the day;
All that is sought shall be accomplished.
Furthermore, if there is anyone who, according to their capacity, hears this True Dharma of the Secret Heart Dhāraṇī of the Sovereign Amogha, it shall likewise be so.
If one can sever all stinginess and jealousy, eliminate every defilement,
and with a pure mind take refuge in and honor the Secret Protectors,
that person shall be counted among the ranks of Bodhisattvas.
They skillfully bring great benefit to sentient beings and shall ultimately attain the fruit of Buddhahood and Bodhi.
World-Honored One, that which is called "Bodhi" is precisely right wisdom (*samyag-prajñā*).
"Sattva" is precisely skillful means.
If one attains such wisdom and is fully endowed with both wisdom and skillful means,
one is then able to perform beneficial deeds for sentient beings.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara again addressed the Buddha,
saying: "World-Honored One, I now wish, in the presence of the Tathāgata,
to proclaim the secret heart-dhāraṇī."
May all fourfold assemblies within this gathering hear it and obtain benefit, peace, and happiness;
may all others who have committed transgressions likewise attain wholesome gain.
The Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Noble Avalokiteśvara, saying:
"O Pure Mahāsattva, you should explain this well; now is the right time.
The Tathāgata shall also express his sympathetic joy today, and even throughout the final age."
He serves as a virtuous refuge for those who practice the Bodhisattva vehicle.
At that time, the noble Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara joyfully raised his eyes to gaze upon the World-Honored One and addressed the Buddha, saying:
The assembly of bodhisattvas here should listen with careful attention and further take refuge;
this wheel of liberation is able to bestow benefit and happiness upon many people.
Out of compassion for the world, performing all manner of great beneficial and joyful deeds,
I now proclaim this dhāraṇī. First,
I take refuge in all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas who dwell well throughout the three periods of time— past, future, and present.
And to all the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas of the three times;
furthermore, I take refuge in the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Amitābha,
and I take refuge in Maitreya and all the other bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
I take refuge in the Greatly Wise Śāriputra and all the Arhats.
Then he spoke this dhāraṇī: *Namo ratnatrayāya*. *Namo 'rha*...
Oṃ āryāvalokiteśvara dṛḍhasattvāya mahāsattvāya mahākāruṇikāya abhiyūna moṣṭrikṛtāya idaṃ āḥ.

The Great Heart Dharani says: *amoghe svāhā*. (1) The Small Heart Dharani says:
*ajite svāhā*. (1) The Heart-of-the-Heart Dharani says: [as follows].
The *vara-pradāya svāhā* mantra for weapons is: *aparājita-ya svāhā*.
The armor mantra (*kavaca-dhāraṇī*) is: *aparājita-ya svāhā*.
Itaṃ karmakuru namoṣṭu ti svāhā. This is the dhāraṇī for the crown of the head.
Oṃ hūṃ jaya svāhā. The uṣṇīṣa-dhāraṇī is as follows:
Oṃ hrīḥ sṭr-ṛ-kya-vijaye amoghapāśāya pratisarā hrīḥ haḥ hūṃ phaṭ. "World-Honored One, this dhāraṇī of mine..."
One will be able to accomplish all undertakings;
for those who constantly maintain this recitation, whatever they do will surely succeed.
Furthermore, even if there is someone who has committed the five heinous crimes of immediate retribution (ānantarya-karma), [they shall be purified].
If that person can recite this dhāraṇī three times each day,
all these karmic obstructions will become completely purified.
If one wishes to perform the rite of boundary-binding (sīmābandha), [one should do so].
One should empower agarwood incense with this dhāraṇī and use it according to the ritual rules.
If one wishes to prohibit malaria,
one should empower ash-water with it.
Alternatively, one may fashion stakes from khadira wood and employ them according to the ritual rules.
If one wishes to pacify all diseases,
one should empower clarified butter, oil, or water, and apply them by means of anointing, rubbing, and so forth.
If one wishes to prohibit the diseases held by the *kākanāsa* spirits,
one should empower a blade according to the ritual rules and employ it.
If one wishes to perform various rites of protection (*paritrāṇa*), [one should do so likewise].
When using the empowered thread according to the ritual,
if one wishes to stop abdominal pain,
one should drink salt water empowered according to the ritual.
If one wishes to pacify various poisons,
one should empower earth or water according to the ritual procedure and employ it.
If one wishes to eliminate eye diseases, [one should do so].
Bind a consecrated white thread around his ear.
If one wishes to remove toothache,
use a consecrated *karañjīra* wood stick as a toothbrush.
Furthermore, for one who wishes to perform the rite of boundary-binding (*sīmābandha*),
one should take threads of five colors and empower them twenty-one times. Then,
using stakes made of khadira wood, one should drive them into the four directions to establish the boundary.
However, by taking a thread and marking out the boundaries with it,
the boundary-binding (sīmābandha) is accomplished.
Furthermore, if one wishes to perform a rite of protection (rakṣāvidhi):
One should empower water, ashes from a cremation ground,
or a pure thread as appropriate. If one wishes to release those who are possessed by spirits, [one should employ these].
Consecrate five-colored thread and employ it according to the ritual rules.
Furthermore, for those who wish to eliminate various types of malarial fevers,
consecrate white thread and employ it according to the ritual rules.
If one wishes to eliminate scrofula and various types of sores or swellings,
one should empower *pippalī* (long pepper), mix it with honey, and apply it by rubbing and other such methods.
Furthermore, if one wishes to remove eye diseases:
Consecrate perfumed water, or licorice water,
or water infused with *prāśa* leaves and use it.
If one wishes to pacify all warfare, strife, and litigation:
One should wash their face with consecrated water.
If one wishes to protect the king’s realm so that it is free from all incursions and disturbances and becomes powerful and victorious, [one should perform this rite].
One should select an exquisite vessel and place it in a clean location;
fill it with water and arrange various offerings.
The practitioner should wear fresh, clean clothing.
Recite this dhāraṇī to perform empowerment.
Then, take water from the flask and sprinkle it everywhere;
immediately the realm will become peaceful and secure, and calamities shall not arise.
It can protect both humans and animals.
If one wishes to dissolve various evil mudrās,
one should take powdered sandalwood incense and empower it twenty-one times.
By touching one's own heart-center, one immediately attains liberation.
If one wishes to perform protection for one's own dwelling,
one should employ a lotus flower in the homa rite.
If one wishes to subdue those who are difficult to subdue,
one should perform the homa rite using sandalwood.
Furthermore, the method for accomplishment is as follows:
One should use superior incense and most excellent incense:
the incense of Abhayapāṇi, the incense of Indrahasta,
the incense of Vāruṇī, and the incense of Nakuli.
The *nākulī* fragrance, *pīlu*, *yūka*, *tagara*,
and so forth, as well as the *candrarāja* medicine, the "Exquisite Joy."
Take the *cakra-bhaiṣajya*,
the *mahā-cakra-bhaiṣajya*, and the *viṣṇu-krandana-bhaiṣajya*;
combine these aforementioned fragrant medicinal substances and form them into a single pill.
If one empowers this dhāraṇī one hundred and eight times,
anyone who is possessed by various ghosts and spirits or is terrified will be protected if they wear it upon their head or upon their arm.
If there is a woman about to give birth,
one should take the aforementioned fragrant medicine, crush it into powder,
empower it according to the ritual rules, and cast it together with water.
When one bathes with this, birth shall occur immediately;
the son of supreme merit will be born in safety and without difficulty,
and all inauspicious matters shall be completely extinguished.
Furthermore, once they have been born, he provides them with excellent protection;
they are freed from all suffering and affliction, and no evil poisons arise.
Should any such things arise, he swiftly dispels them.
If one wishes to provide protection for a newborn infant,
take the aforementioned incense pills and empower them according to the ritual method;
by wearing them upon the crown of the head, protection will be secured.
If one wishes to prohibit wind, clouds, thunder, and hail,
one should take a branch of the Varuṇī tree,
place it in pure water, and empower it according to the ritual rules.
Next, grasp its branch and sprinkle [the water] with it.
"World-Honored One, this secret heart-dhāraṇī of mine is capable of bringing about the most supreme accomplishment."
All the functions of the dharmas as described above are entirely unfailing.
Even those who have not yet mastered the recitation will attain accomplishment.
Furthermore, the method for accomplishing the *iṣṭadevatā* (honored deity) shall now be proclaimed.
If anyone desires to see my body and seek accomplishment, they should,
on the fifteenth day of the waxing moon, prepare a painting according to the ritual rules.
Using excellent, unmixed pigments, they should paint my image.
He has the appearance of Maheśvara,
wearing a jeweled crown with a deerskin draped over his shoulder,
and adorned with all manner of precious gems.
Having thus completed the painting, one should arrange it according to the ritual rules.
The practitioner should then prepare a maṇḍala out of cow dung before that painted image.
They scattered various exquisite flowers and established offerings of eight kinds of incense.
Furthermore, they arranged sixty-four varieties of prepared food and drink,
all of which were pure, free from blood, meat, raw fish, and any impurities.
Burn aloeswood incense.
The practitioner should refrain from eating for day and night.
Three times each day, they should bathe their body and put on fresh, clean garments.
Having made offerings with a mind of focused concentration,
recite this dhāraṇī one thousand and eighty times before the painted image. Then,
clearly visualize the form and characteristics of the deity.
Then one sees that one's own body is ablaze with great flames.
Upon seeing this, the practitioner gives rise to joy in their heart.
In a brief moment, they see my body appear before them.
One should grant all that is requested so that it is entirely fulfilled.
At that time, the practitioner should use realgar or the medicinal substance añjana to apply as an ointment to the eyes.
One is then able to conceal one's body and also ascend into the air,
freely entering the samādhi door of the Adornment of Non-Empty Wisdom;
whatever one desires and whatever one undertakes, all shall be perfectly fulfilled.
When the Buddha had finished speaking this sutra,
the Holy Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara,
along with the other Īśvaras, Maheśvaras, and the assembly of Brahmā deities, [rejoiced].

The Pure Light Devaputra, along with all the bodhisattvas, śrāvakas, and the entire great assembly, having heard what the Buddha had spoken, were all greatly rejoiced; they believed, accepted, and practiced it accordingly.
Thus concludes the *Sūtra on the Secret Heart Dhāraṇī of the Holy Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, the Sovereign King of Non-Vainness*.
